channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-25
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 105 news received.

item.title: 1. Trump and Silicon Valley convinced Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back
item.description: Why it matters: The reported political and Silicon Valley pressure on Nvidia’s leadership signals potentially significant implications for the company’s strategy, valuation, and U.S. technology policy. The article explains how Donald Trump and Silicon Valley pushed Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back.

item.title: 2. CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
item.description: Why it matters: CrowdStrike’s proposed $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler would reshape the cybersecurity market by combining endpoint, cloud, identity, and zero-trust capabilities. CrowdStrike announced the all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing together endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security and threat intelligence. Jay Chaudhry will remain CEO of Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.

item.title: 3. Anthropic launches Claude Ship to automate code approvals
item.description: Why it matters: Anthropic’s Claude Ship moves AI coding agents closer to autonomous software delivery by letting them review, fix, and approve code within enterprise GitHub workflows. Claude Ship brings together agents that can review code, fix issues, and automatically approve certain changes. The service is being rolled out in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub repositories.

item.title: 4. The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
item.description: Why it matters: The EU Chips Act’s €33 billion investment package materially strengthens Europe’s semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, and power-electronics capacity. Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.

item.title: 5. OpenAI’s chief scientist calls for limiting the pace of AI progress
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s chief scientist calling for common limits on the pace of AI progress elevates frontier-model safety from an internal concern to a potential industry-wide governance issue. Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores for every major model since GPT-3.5 and is asking competing labs to agree on common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.
